newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba offical calls for redoubled savings efforts.
newsitem.headline: Buba offical calls for redoubled savings efforts.

text.p: Germany must redouble its efforts to reduce its budget deficit in order to meet strict entry requirements for the planned single European currency, a senior Bundesbank official said on Friday.

Hans-Juergen Koebnick, a council member and also president of the state central bank of Rhineland-Palatinate and the Saar regions, told ZDF German television, "In my view we must step up our efforts (to consolidate debt)."
The European economic and monetary union is scheduled to begin on January 1, 1999, with those nations whose budget deficits do not exceed three percent of gross domestic product.
Koebnick said the steps that had already been initiated to pare back deficits and government debt were headed in the right direction but must be strengthened further.

He re-emphasised that Germany would likely miss meeting the three percent target this year, and forecast that the budget deficit may be closer to four percent of GDP than last year's 3.5 percent rate.
He also said that it remains unclear whether Germany "can reach the ambitious three percent goal next year in light of all the existing uncertainties."
